author: BBC News
description:
Internet and call services have been disrupted in Ethiopia's northern region of Tigray following the outbreak of fighting this week between regional forces and the national army.
 
Sources have told the Reuters news agency that the group which controls Tigray, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), ordered the communications blackout, with one suggesting it was to disrupt government drones.
 
The TPLF has not commented.
 
The BBC is unable to report from Tigray and surrounding areas.
 
Even before the current disruption, finding video and images to establish what is happening on the ground has been a challenge.

author: BBC News
description:
The Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light moved into a former orphanage in Crewe, Cheshire, in 2021. Its American-born leader, Abdullah Hashem, claims to be the Mahdi, a messianic figure regarded in Islam as the saviour of mankind.

Earlier this year, around 500 police officers raided the organisation's headquarters as part of an investigation into allegations of forced marriage, modern slavery and sexual offences.

In this episode of BBC News: Behind the Investigation, journalists Hayley Mortimer and Emir Nader explain how they investigated the group's journey from Egypt to Germany, Sweden and ultimately the UK. They discuss the beliefs of the movement, its controversial leader, the disappearance of a former member, and the challenges of reporting on a new religious movement.

To hear the full investigation, search for File on 4 Investigates on BBC Sounds or wherever you get your podcasts.

Background to the police investigation:
https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c759n2lnxz0o

#BBCNew
title: Has a cult come to town? Behind The Investigation | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
South Africa's new ambassador to Washington, Roelf Meyer, has a personal reason to challenge US President Donald Trump's assertion that there is a genocide against white Afrikaners - he is "a born Afrikaner" himself.
 
The notion of a mass attack on the white Afrikaner minority in South Africa does not exist, he told the BBC, adding that his identity gave him the legitimacy to say so.
 
Meyer was one of the chief mediators to end white-minority rule known as apartheid in South Africa in the 1990s, and he was appointed ambassador to the US in April, after diplomatic relations between the US and South Africa plummeted.
 
In an interview with the BBC, Meyer said the facts about violence in South Africa had been misrepresented and he never got a clear answer about where this "misdirection of information" was coming from.
 
Last year, Trump accused South Africa of white genocide in a meeting with President Cyril Ramaphosa at the White House and launched a US refugee pathway for Afrikaners.
title: Examining ‘white genocide’ claims in South Africa | BBC News

description:
Massive floods and landslides swept through border towns and villages in Nepal and Tibet a month ago, wiping out thousands of houses and destroying energy infrastructure.
 
Since then, 1,400 people are known to have died, thousands are still missing and many are displaced.
 
Scientists say the floods were caused by a collapse of rock wall and glacier ice near the peak of Langtang Lirung, a mountain on Nepal's side of the Himalayas.

author: BBC News
description:
Manchester City may be expelled from the Premier League after being found guilty of the vast majority of of 115 breaches of the financial rules it had been accused of. 

Sanctions on the club, which are yet to be announced, may include exclusion from the UK’s top football league, a points deduction or a huge fine. 

The news of the guilty verdict was broken by the Athletic, which reported that 114 of the 115 charges have been upheld.  The BBC has been told that the club is planning to appeal. 

The news came 1,327 days after City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 following a four-year investigation, and 22 months since a hearing by an independent commission concluded.

The seismic decisions leaves a huge number of questions about what will happen next, what City's punishment might be and how the current season will be affected.

One possibility is that rival Premier League sides may take legal action for compensation, claiming they have been impacted by City's action
title: MAN CITY FOUND GUILTY - club may be expelled from Premier League for financial cheating | BBC News
